name: Expense Policy Check
description: Audit 10 to 26 expense claim lines from several employees against a written policy: receipts from £25.00, alcohol, daily meal limits by city shared across several meals, hotel limits per night, client entertainment per head unless the approval is in the director register, first-class rail, mileage at 45p then 25p after 10,000 miles in the tax year (crossing the 6 April reset), a 60-day submission limit, duplicates, euro and dollar conversion and VAT reclaim rules. The answer is the non-compliant lines with the rule broken and the amount to pay, totals per employee, the grand total and the reclaimable VAT, to the penny.
hook: Twenty-six claim lines, one policy, every penny checked. Who gets paid what?
author: Gauntlet Core

cases.prompt:
I run the monthly expenses check. Please audit this batch of claim lines against our policy and tell me what to pay.

Expenses policy (Finance, version 7) — apply every rule exactly as written.

A. Conversion. Amounts in euros or US dollars are converted to pounds at the rate in the rate table, rounded to the nearest penny, BEFORE any limit is applied. All limits are in pounds.
B. Rules, in this order. A line breaks a rule when that rule reduces what the company pays for it.
 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved in writing (rule 7).
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a daily limit per employee per day, by city: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. When one employee has several meals on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that day's limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included). If, and only if, the line's approval reference appears in the Director approvals register below, the whole amount is paid, alcohol included. An approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register does not count.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that. The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order, starting from the miles already paid in the tax year named on their claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
C. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full are compliant and must not be listed.
D. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.

Rate table: €1 = £0.87, $1 = £0.74.

Director approvals register (written approvals for client entertainment):

  L02 | Fri 5 Jun 2026 | Kirkgate Market Diner, Leeds | Lunch | £37.19 | VAT £6.20 | receipt attached
  L03 | Thu 11 Jun 2026 | National Rail (LNER/Avanti/GWR) | Rail Manchester Piccadilly – Glasgow Central return, standard class | £58.90 | receipt attached
  L04 | Fri 12 Jun 2026 | Black cab | Taxi to client site | £31.50 | no receipt
  L05 | Tue 9 Jun 2026 | Royal Mail | Special Delivery postage | £14.20 | no receipt
  L06 | Fri 5 Jun 2026 | National Rail (LNER/Avanti/GWR) | Rail London Euston – Glasgow Central return, standard class | £120.10 | receipt attached

Claim C-3629 — Elif Patel (Operations), submitted Mon 29 Jun 2026. Business miles already paid in tax year 2026/27 before this claim: 800.
  L07 | Thu 25 Jun 2026 | Kirkgate Market Diner, Leeds | Breakfast | £34.80 | includes alcohol £9.50 | VAT £5.80 | receipt attached
  L08 | Fri 26 Jun 2026 | Harbourside Inn Bristol, Bristol | Hotel, 1 night | £80.80 | VAT £13.47 | receipt attached
  L09 | Thu 25 Jun 2026 | High Street Pharmacy | First-aid kit restock | £20.91 | VAT £3.49 | receipt attached
  L10 | Thu 16 Apr 2026 | Own car | Mileage, 318 miles (client visits) | £143.10 | no receipt needed
  L11 | Tue 23 Jun 2026 | City Car Parks | Parking, client visit | £21.55 | VAT £3.59 | receipt attached
  L12 | Fri 12 Jun 2026 | National Rail (LNER/Avanti/GWR) | Rail London Euston – Glasgow Central return, standard class | £120.10 | receipt attached

Answer with one JSON object in exactly this shape:
{"non_compliant": {"L03": {"rule": "HOTEL_CAP", "pay": 360.00}, "L07": {"rule": "NO_RECEIPT", "pay": 0}, ...}, "pay_by_employee": {"Full Name": 512.40, "Other Name": 98.10, ...}, "total_pay": 610.50, "vat_reclaimable": 41.27}
- non_compliant: one entry per line that is paid less than claimed, keyed by line number, with the rule (one of LATE, DUPLICATE, NO_RECEIPT, ALCOHOL, MEAL_CAP, HOTEL_CAP, ENTERTAINMENT_CAP, RAIL_CLASS, MILEAGE_RATE) and the amount to pay in pounds. Do not list lines that are paid in full.
- pay_by_employee: the total to pay each employee (every employee in the batch); total_pay: the total for the batch; vat_reclaimable: the total VAT the company can reclaim.
All amounts in pounds to the penny (a £ sign and thousands separators are fine). Marking: each listed line earns a point for the rule and a point for the amount; every line you list that should not be listed costs two points; each total is a point. Reply with the JSON object only (a ```json code block is fine); key order, spacing and letter case do not matter. Give one value per field: a field with two values is marked wrong, and if you give more than one JSON answer only the last one counts.

 1. LATE — a line whose expense date is more than 60 days before its claim's submission date pays £0.
 2. DUPLICATE — the same expense claimed again (same employee, date, merchant and amount, in the same or another claim): the later line (higher line number) pays £0.
 3. NO_RECEIPT — any line of £25.00 or more (after conversion) without a receipt pays £0. Mileage needs no receipt.
 4. ALCOHOL — alcohol is never paid (deduct the alcohol amount shown on the line, converted if needed), except on client entertainment approved in writing (rule 7).
 5. MEAL_CAP — meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) are paid up to a daily limit per employee per day, by city: London £40, other UK cities £30, Paris £48, Dublin £44, New York £60. When one employee has several meals on the same day, take them in line order: each is paid up to what is left of that day's limit (after any alcohol deduction).
 6. HOTEL_CAP — hotels are paid up to a limit per night: London £180, other UK cities £120, Paris £190, Dublin £170, New York £240.
 7. ENTERTAINMENT_CAP — client entertainment is paid up to £60 per head (count everyone at the table, staff included). If, and only if, the line's approval reference appears in the Director approvals register below, the whole amount is paid, alcohol included. An approval mentioned on a claim but missing from the register does not count.
 8. RAIL_CLASS — rail travel is paid at standard class: a first-class ticket is paid at the standard fare shown on the line.
 9. MILEAGE_RATE — business mileage in a private car is paid at 45p a mile for the first 10,000 business miles in the tax year and 25p a mile after that. The tax year runs 6 April to 5 April. Count each employee's miles in date order, starting from the miles already paid in the tax year named on their claim (in any other tax year, start from 0); a journey that crosses 10,000 is split. Mileage is paid at the correct rate whatever amount was claimed.
C. Report a line as non-compliant when it is paid less than its claimed amount (in pounds). Give the FIRST rule in the list above that reduced it, and the amount to pay. Lines paid in full are compliant and must not be listed.
D. VAT. The company reclaims the VAT shown on a line only if the line is paid in full, is in pounds (a UK expense), has a receipt and is not client entertainment. Mileage carries no VAT.
